_what: Volunteers (love.css §130), a shopfront on the street: a cloth on the loom, half woven, with the window behind the warp. Ryan's brief, 2026-10-27: a Volunteers room, its channel on the CB under Community on the chat page, borrowing from stimpunks.org's Volunteer page. tools/make-volunteers.py writes the loom, every section, the help list, the playbooks, the rules, the channel, next door and the credits out of this file.
_the_cloth: The warp is our values and runs unbroken through every band; the weft is what each person brings, a band of its own colour. A woven cloth holds because every thread grips the ones it crosses: the friction our Volunteer page says we exist as is the thing that holds a weave together. The page's own picture of our interdependence is rainbow woven cloth. Every dye is a natural dye named for what it is made from, and no two bands that touch are the same dye.
_read: Every quotation and every holds line was read on our own pages in the Knowledge System mirror on 2026-10-27, and is checked against it word for word on every build where the mirror is on the machine.

lede.p: This room is a cloth on the loom, half woven. The warp runs up from it to the beam, all one undyed thread: that is what has to fit. Across it, band by band, is the weft, a colour for every person and every thing they brought. Above the newest row the warp is bare and the window shows between the threads, and the shuttle is lying on the cloth with the next thread on it.
A woven cloth holds because every thread grips the ones it crosses. No single thread carries the cloth, and none of them is holding it alone. Load-sharing is what weaving is.

Its channel on the CB is for volunteering with Stimpunks: asking what needs doing, offering what you can, and finding the people doing the same thing. Sign on and tune the radio to **This room** while you are in here, or open [Volunteers on the chat page](chat.html#volunteers), under Community. If you are not on the CB yet, [the Community Center](community-center.html#getting-started) says how to get an invite.

warp.p: The warp goes on the loom first and stays the same from one end of the cloth to the other. Before you volunteer, get to know who we are and what we hold to, and ask yourself whether it fits:

A values fit and not a culture fit. The weft can be any colour at all; it is the warp that has to be shared. And everybody on the CB, volunteering or not, keeps [our covenant](https://stimpunks.org/covenant/), which is a floor and not a ceiling:

weft.p: These are the things our Volunteer page says we need help with, each a band in the cloth. Pick up whichever thread you like, as much or as little of it as you have.

ecology.p: Nobody here is a cog in somebody else’s machine. What we are building is an ecology of care: people with different gifts, joined by trust, each doing the part that suits them and leaning on the others for the rest. Our Volunteer page leans on the Autistic Collaboration Trust for this, and so does this room.

roles.p: Our Volunteer page asks you to think about which of its roles you relate to, or would like to: Weavers, Experimenters, Frontline Responders, Visionaries, Builders, Caregivers, Disruptors, Healers, Storytellers and Guides. Each is defined in [the map itself](https://buildingmovement.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/Ecosystem-Guide-2020.pdf), in the words of the people who made it. This is the one that names what a loom is for:

playbooks.p: As a shorthand for the ways there are to help, our Volunteer page borrows four playbooks from [Human Restoration Project](https://www.humanrestorationproject.org). Most people are in more than one, and you do not have to choose.

form.p: Volunteering starts with [the volunteer form on our Volunteer page](https://stimpunks.org/volunteer/#h-volunteer-form), on stimpunks.org. It asks how to reach you, your social media if you would like to share it, what you are interested in and how you could help, and it shows you what you wrote before you send it. Nothing in this room takes your details: the form is the way in, and the channel is for talking.

What you send comes to [our office](privacy.html#office) as a volunteer application, sealed where it is kept, and only our directors, board members and administrators can open it. They are a tiny team, they cannot move at the speed of emergencies, and sometimes they take a week or two off. If you have not heard from us in a week, ask again.

not_here.name: Nobody counts.
not_here.line: No hours logged, no tally of who did what, no volunteer of the month, nothing ranked. A cloth does not keep a list of which thread did the most.

not_here.name: Nobody owes time.
not_here.line: Joining the channel commits you to nothing. You can say no, put a thread down half way, step back for as long as you need and pick it up again, and nobody asks why.

not_here.name: Rest is not quitting.
not_here.line: We exist as friction and it is exhausting, and that is true of the people helping too. When you are running on empty, [Dead Tired Society](dead-tired-society.html) and [the Healing Checkpoint](healing-checkpoint.html) are on the street.

not_here.name: Nobody is a hero, and nobody is a cause.
not_here.line: We work with each other and alongside each other, not for anybody. Nobody here is selfless, and nobody we work with is anybody's good deed.

not_here.name: Nothing here takes your details.
not_here.line: The volunteer form is on stimpunks.org. This room has no form, no box and no sign-up sheet.
